method: Classification is by STATE DELTA, never by tactic name. This project measured MI(head; effect)/H(head) = 0.240 over 259,580 steps: an operation name carries only 24% of the information about what it does to the state, so selecting witnesses by tactic name would select the wrong steps.

P02.question: Does HML need an in-place claim-transformation primitive?
P02.headline: 462 of 5,000 sampled steps (9.24%) rebind the SAME hypothesis name to a DIFFERENT proposition. Top heads: rw 135, obtain 40, have 34, simp 29, rcases 28, replace 18. In-place transformation is real and common.
P02.information_lost: None that is truth-relevant. Original proposition, transformed proposition, derivational relationship, dependencies, warrant, scope and historical trajectory are all retained. HML does not reproduce Lean's DISCARDING of the old hypothesis, which is tactic ergonomics.

adversarial_case.shape: hr : forall j, r j k -> ... becomes hr : forall j, r j i -> ..., and the VARIABLE k is itself removed from the context
adversarial_case.finding: A genuine divergence: preserving the old claim preserves a proposition mentioning a binder the after-state no longer has.
adversarial_case.why_it_does_not_motivate_the_addition: HML models propositions as opaque strings with no binder structure at all. An in-place mutation primitive would not represent variable elimination either. This is a modelling boundary, not a missing channel.

P02.decision: CLOSED. Immutable derive-new is sufficient on current evidence; destructive in-place mutation is not required and is actively refused by the frame condition. No parent_fact_id, no version id, no SUPERSEDES, no mutation channel.
P02.correction: D-055 said 'derive-new + supersede is already expressible today'. The second half is FALSE and is withdrawn. ClaimStatus has no value marking a claim superseded, deletion is refused by the frame, and the only mechanism making a fact non-citable is scope closure — a statement about frames, not about one fact superseding another. HML DOES NOT REPRESENT SUPERSESSION.

P03.question: Does SemanticState lose mathematically relevant subgoal-ancestry information?
P03.headline: Lean genuinely creates goals: 18,315 of 259,580 steps (7.06%) have delta_goals > 0, and 18,901 (7.28%) leave more than one goal. Our own corpus has ZERO goal-creating transitions in 631, so it could not have answered this.
P03.multi_goal_before_note: 1,592 / 259,580 — reproduces D-056's independently derived 0.61% exactly. LeanDojo traces the FOCUSED goal, so the tree is far more visible in state_after (7.28%) than in state_before.
P03.current_hml_result: Goal creation is NOT REPRESENTABLE: no action can declare that it creates subgoals, and Goal carries only id/proposition/status/scope — no parent field. Before D-057 the verifier ACCEPTED unlicensed goal creation, deletion and mutation silently; it now fails closed.
P03.information_lost: Ancestry is moot while goal creation itself has no vocabulary: there is no parent-child relation to lose because no transition can express one. This is a sharper finding than 'ancestry is deferred'.
P03.decision: DEFERRED — SOURCE_CANNOT_ADJUDICATE is NOT the reason. The external source adjudicates it clearly: Lean has the structure, HML cannot express it. A parent_goal_id remains unjustified because the field it would hang from does not exist; adding ancestry before goal creation would be a pointer with nothing to point at. No GoalTree, no planner, no scheduler.
